# `response-success-status-added`

New 1xx/2xx/3xx response

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` |
| **Rule IDs** | `response-success-status-added` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Responses ([RULES.md section 6](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new 1xx, 2xx or 3xx response, e.g. `202` alongside `200`, or `304`.

## Why this default

Clients may only handle the statuses they knew about and treat the new one as an error. It's a warning because many clients accept any 2xx.

## Example

From test case [`response-success-status-added`](../../test/cases/response-success-status-added/): A new 2xx alongside 200 is a warning.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
                schema:
                  type: object
+         '202':
+           description: accepted
```

Findings:

- `response-success-status-added` · warn · GET /pets

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ignore-statuses` | `[]` | Statuses that never warn when added, e.g. `[202, 204]`. |

```yaml
rules:
  response-success-status-added: warn
```

## How to fix

Only return the new status to clients that opt in (e.g. with a `Prefer` header), or document it clearly.
